newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Strong U.S. data prompts flight from Belgian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Strong U.S. data prompts flight from Belgian bonds.

text.p: A spate of strong jobs and price figures from the United States knocked the Belgian linear bond market lower on Friday, and traders said they expected caution to prevail next week ahead of news on the German repo rate.
"Today everything came from the United States," one trader said. "The first impact was from the non-farm payroll figures and this was followed by the NAPM price index."
The July non-farm payroll figure rose 316,000, far more than had been expected.
The National Association of Purchasing Managers July price index was 53.6 against 48.1 in June.
Traders said the strong figures triggered a tide of selling in Belgium as well as in other European markets and the United States.
"There were some big sellers of Belgian paper," one trader said. "People saw it as a good opportunity to sell Belgium."
However, as is usual on a sharp down move, Belgian paper outperformed its German counterpart and the spread over Bunds narrowed.
In the 10-year benchmark Belgian OLO the spread narrowed at one stage to seven basis points before settling at eight -- one basis point lower that Thursday's close.
The yield of the benchmark linear bond ended at 5.68 percent against Thursday's 5.62.
Traders noted there had been a tendency to buy Belgian paper when the spread widened to 10 basis points and sell it when it fell to seven.

However, caution would likely hold back the market before it becomes clear whether the German Bundesbank will announce a variable repo rate -- in effect a rate rise -- or a two-tier repo in the next 10-days.
Another factor in the Belgian bond market on Friday was a further decline in money market rates.
The one-week repo rate fell to 3.55/65 percent from Thursday's 3.80/85.
Traders said there was as little explanation for the sudden reversal in money rates as there had been for the sudden surge earlier this week.

However, they noted the Belgian Treasury had taken less paper than came to maturity at the weekly T-bill auction on Tuesday and some 30 billion francs of OLO coupon payments come due on Saturday to add to the 50 billion earlier in the week.
